report.summary: Payments became stuck in PENDING because the ledger database volume ran completely out of disk space, resulting in PostgreSQL write failures ('No space left on device') starting at 13:52 UTC. This caused ledger-service and payments-api to fail database INSERT operations and mark payments for retry.

supporting.note: Shows disk usage upward anomaly starting at 13:19 UTC and saturating at 100.7% at 13:59 UTC.
Shows ledger-db warning for disk usage at 96% at 13:22 UTC.
Shows explicit PostgreSQL disk full errors starting at 13:52 UTC.
Shows ledger-db error rate rising sharply at 13:52 UTC.
Shows ledger-service logging PSQLException 'No space left on device' during INSERT operations starting at 13:52 UTC.
Shows ledger-service error rate spiking at 13:52 UTC.
Shows payments-api marking payments as PENDING for retry starting at 13:53 UTC due to ledger write failures.
Shows kyc-service was deployed at 14:00 UTC, aligning with the reported timing in the incident summary.

contradicting.note: Ledger-db disk exhaustion and write errors started at 13:52 UTC, which is 8 minutes before the kyc-service deployment.
Ledger-service disk errors started at 13:52 UTC.
Ledger-service error rates started rising at 13:52 UTC.
Payments-api error rates started rising at 13:53 UTC.

facts.text: Ledger-db disk_used_pct showed an upward anomaly starting at 2026-10-03T13:19:00+00:00 and reached a saturated peak of 100.7% at 13:59:00+00:00.
Ledger-db logged warning for disk usage at 96% starting at 2026-10-03T13:22:49+00:00.
Ledger-service error rate and latency anomalies started at 2026-10-03T13:52:00+00:00.
Ledger-service logged disk full errors during INSERT operations starting at 2026-10-03T13:52:00+00:00.
Ledger-db error_rate_pct increased sharply from its baseline of 0.05% starting at 2026-10-03T13:52:00+00:00.
Ledger-db logged database extension errors (No space left on device) starting at 2026-10-03T13:52:08+00:00.
Payments-api error rates started rising at 2026-10-03T13:53:00+00:00.
Payments-api began logging ledger write failures and marking payments as PENDING for retry at 2026-10-03T13:53:03+00:00.
Kyc-service was deployed to version v5.2.0 via chg-9369 at 2026-10-03T14:00:00+00:00.

assumptions: The underlying storage volume reached maximum capacity due to natural data accumulation or database growth without an explicit prior administrative failure log.
The timestamps of ledger-db and ledger-service errors occurring 8 minutes prior to the deploy are coincidental.

timeline.event: Ledger-db disk usage upward anomaly begins
Ledger-db logs warning for disk usage at 96%
Ledger-service and ledger-db begin experiencing disk full write errors and error rate spikes
Payments-api error rate rises and payments are marked PENDING for retry
Ledger-db disk usage reaches saturated peak of 100.7%

recommended_actions.action: Immediately expand the storage volume backing ledger-db to restore write operations.
recommended_actions.rationale: Ledger-db is completely out of disk space (100.7%), causing database write failures and leaving payments stuck in PENDING.

recommended_actions.action: Implement automated recovery mechanisms and retry processing for payments stuck in PENDING once ledger-db storage is expanded.
recommended_actions.rationale: Hundreds of payments were marked as PENDING for retry due to ledger write failures and will need reconciliation.

recommended_actions.action: Set up proactive storage utilization alerts and automated volume scaling for ledger-db before disk usage reaches critical thresholds like 90%.
recommended_actions.rationale: Disk usage warnings at 96% were logged well before complete saturation, indicating a need for better capacity monitoring and early alerting.
